outs.ratioText#14: On a per-customer basis: winning a new customer costs 5.0× what it costs to keep one you already have. The turnover of a rep serving 250 customers adds about $62.4 of hidden cost per customer (that's 69% of the retention cost). In absolute terms one agent's departure still costs $15,600 — the equivalent of acquiring 35 new customers. The through-line: retention — of both customers and staff — is the cheapest dollar you spend.
outs.doorText#27: Losing one customer to poor service really costs about $13,650 — not the $2,400 sale, but the lifetime margin, the $450 to replace them, and the referrals that never come. At 18% churn on 320 customers, that's $786,240 walking out the door every year — and you have to win 58 new customers just to break even before you grow at all. Spending $5,184 to keep that same group instead protects $304,128 of value — a 59× return. And the two doors are connected: an experienced, well-treated CSR is what keeps that churn number low — lose the rep, service slips, and the customer door starts spinning faster.
